summary: CORS preflight OPTIONS requests appear counted against tenant quota during bulk embed uploads via CDN signed URLs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated 429s that coincide with large bulk-embed uploads performed through CDN-signed URLs. Customer asserts that a disproportionate number of quota increments correspond to CORS preflight (OPTIONS) requests, not the actual PUT/POST embed payloads.

Impact:
- Several bulk ingestion jobs (~600 parallel workers) intermittently fail with 429.
- Observed token/quota decrement patterns appear to correlate with bursts of OPTIONS preflights in the same time window.
- Customer sees billing/usage lines that appear to attribute API calls to their tenant during preflight spikes.

Environment:
- prod/us-east
- Customer tier: self_serve
- Integration path: client -> CDN (signed URL) -> edge proxy -> api-gateway -> embedding service

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Generate short-lived signed URLs for PUT upload of document chunks.
2) Client performs CORS preflight (OPTIONS) for each target origin before PUT.
3) Parallel clients (hundreds) run with default browsers / worker scripts, causing many OPTIONS to fire in a window.
4) Bulk job intermittently receives 429s and upload orchestration marks chunks as failed.

Observed behavior:
- OPTIONS requests appear in traffic logs and a matching number of quota-meter increments are visible in the console for the tenant during the same window.
- Sample request-ids: req-20260310-az12-45f3, req-20260310-az12-46b7. Edge logs show METHOD=OPTIONS and route=/v1/embeddings/upload-chunk.
- Console "tokens consumed" graph shows spikes aligned to these windows and not fully explainable by the size/number of subsequent PUTs.

Expected behavior:
- CORS preflight (OPTIONS) should not count toward token/usage quota for embed generation endpoints; only the actual embed POST/PUT that contains the payload should be billed.

Attachments:
- Customer supplied a short anonymized HAR and a CSV of request timestamps.
- Edge proxy request snippets (redacted) included in comments.

Additional notes:
- Customer changed client to group uploads behind a single signed URL and saw a reduction in OPTIONS frequency; problem reduced but persisted.
- Customer requests explanation, temporary mitigation, and guidance on client settings (Access-Control-Max-Age, single-signed-url patterns) to avoid future quota impact.
steps_to_reproduce: Generate signed URLs for each chunk upload via client
Trigger browser-based preflights (OPTIONS) for each signed-url target
Run 300-600 parallel workers uploading small chunks
Observe 429s and quota spikes in console

investigation_notes: Edge proxy logs show meter increment events containing route-id and method. Example: meter_inc{route='emb-upload', method='OPTIONS', tenant='brightdata'}.

Rate-accounting filter matches by normalized path (signed-url token is stripped) and currently increments per-request regardless of HTTP method. This behavior causes OPTIONS preflights to be treated as billable requests for some upload routes.
Staging repro confirmed: high parallel OPTIONS load triggers tenant token-bucket depletion and 429s on subsequent PUT requests when backpressure is applied by quota layer.

No evidence of billing-service double-counting; increments are surfaced early at gateway/edge meter. Billing rows later reflect those increments, which is why customer saw usage lines align with preflight windows.

A/B flag introduced in CDN to 'forward_preflight_to_origin' was toggled for a subset of customers last month; BrightData landed on the active cohort and experienced increased preflight forwarding. Need to audit the rollout flags for other tenants.
Suggested temporary mitigation: increase Access-Control-Max-Age at origin, consolidate signed URLs, stagger worker startup, or use server-side upload aggregation to avoid browser preflight noise.
resolution_notes: Engineering to deploy a patch to rate-accounting filter to ignore OPTIONS and HEAD methods for route-based quota increments (planned rollout 2026-03-18).
Audit CDN forward_preflight_to_origin rollout and roll back for affected self-serve tenants if necessary.
Customer guidance provided on Access-Control-Max-Age and grouping signed URLs; customer reports partial improvement and will monitor until server-side fix is live.
Follow-up: create INT ticket to add automated test coverage for method-exclusion in quota accounting and a postmortem runbook entry for signed-url + preflight interaction.
